item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is preferable because its API errors and retry test are stronger, although both patches violate the explicit requirement to implement Upload by delegating to FilesService.Add.","reasons":["A’s retry test parses the multipart body and verifies file content on every attempt, directly proving that streamed content survives replay; B only counts requests and never reads either retried body.","A reports empty filename and nil content independently, producing more precise API errors than B’s combined validation message.","A adds practical user documentation while clearly preserving Add as the lower-level API.","Both correctly reuse multipartbody.NewFile, preserve the requested signature, use the field name \"file\", and propagate helper errors."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), contrary to the frozen contract.","The visible tests do not cover empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, or source-reader failures as explicitly required.","The added non-replayable Add test and extensive documentation increase scope somewhat beyond the core API addition."],"risks_b":["Like A, Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its machinery, creating future semantic-drift risk.","The retry test does not verify multipart filename, field, or content on the retried request, so it provides weak evidence of body replay.","The visible tests omit validation and source-reader failure coverage required by the contract, and the combined validation error is less specific."]}
